key_insight: SARAH is the first fully causal, real-time system that makes conversational virtual agents spatially aware—using user position + dyadic audio to produce natural full-body motion and gaze that responds to a live interlocutor.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between speech-aligned gesture generation and spatially grounded social behavior: current methods ignore user location and dynamics or require non-causal/offline processing, preventing natural, low-latency interactions in VR and telepresence.
method: Causal, real-time motion generation that conditions on live user 3D position and dyadic audio to produce full-body motion and gaze
Architectural design and training regime optimized for streaming VR headsets (low-latency inference and deployable on-device/edge)
Behavioral priors that encode turning, gaze, and proxemic responses so agents react naturally to user movement without future context
impact: Enables more believable, responsive digital humans for VR, telepresence, and mixed-reality apps by adding spatial awareness while meeting strict latency and deployability constraints—lowering the barrier to real-world interactive agent deployment.
visual_elements: System diagram: inputs (user 3D position + dyadic audio) → SARAH model → live avatar motion + gaze
Before/After side-by-side: non-spatial vs spatially-aware agent reacting to a moving user
Performance panel: latency and throughput bars showing real-time streaming viability on VR headset
Behavior overlays: 3D pose/gaze heatmap demonstrating turning and proxemic responses
paper_title: SARAH: Spatially Aware Real-time Agentic Humans
paper_authors: Evonne Ng, Siwei Zhang, Zhang Chen, Michael Zollhoefer, Alexander Richard
